sentences.text: The petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 are before this Court calling in question proceedings in S.C.No.92/2021, pending before the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere, for the offences punishable under Sections 506, 498A, 504, 323, 354B r/w. 34 of the IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 in unison submit that during the pendency of these proceedings, the parties to the lis have settled their matrimonial dispute amicably by drawing up certain terms and conditions.

They have decided to live together with their kids and therefore, filed an application under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C. r/w. 359 of the BNSS, 2023, and separate affidavits of the parties, before this Court to that effect.
NC: 2026:KHC:6082 HC-KAR 3.

The affidavit of the complainant reads as follows:
"I submit that I am the respondent No.2 in the above petition.

I submit that on my complaint the Davanagere women Police on the basis of the said complaint registered a case in Crime No.90/2019 against the petitioners for the offence punishable under section 498A, 323, 504, 506, 354A r/w. 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P.Act.

I submit that at the intervention of the elders, family friends and well wishers the above case has been settled amicably between the said parties and both myself and the 1st petitioner are living happily along with my child and we are living happily and hence this settlement is arrived between us.

I submits that we declare that the settlement has been reached by mutual discussions and amicably, without any undue force, influence, coercion, misrepresentation or fraud and with free consent and will of both the parties an we all living happily."

In the light of the fact that the parties have arrived at settlement and living happily together and since it is a marital dispute, I deem it appropriate to accept the application and the separate affidavits of the parties and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are Sri Vinay T M vs State Of Karnataka on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36140735/
3 not against the State.

ORDER (i) The criminal petition is disposed.
(ii) The proceedings in S.C.No.92/2021, pending before the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere, stand quashed.
